22.0.0.en: 1- My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?

22.0.1.en: The words of my roaring: words coming out with my breath, that is, my sighs; for roaring is the air that goes out when a person breathes.

22.0.2.en: 1- This verse clearly applies to Christ, because He said it on the Cross. It is a clear prophecy of His sufferings, which David saw by the spirit of prophecy.

22.0.3.en: 2- These words confirm the humanity of Christ, who truly suffered severe pain and expresses it by His cry to God, and confirms it by saying "my God" twice; that is, Christ took a real body like the rest of mankind.

22.0.4.en: 3- In His saying "my God" the boldness of sonship appears; for He speaks to God on behalf of humanity as a man. And although He suffers from the intensity of the pain and says "thou hast forsaken me", at the same time He expresses the faith and the boldness that exist between Him and the Father, or as every spiritual person ought to behave with boldness toward God.

22.0.5.en: 4- This verse is an expression of the purity and holiness of God, who cannot bear sin, which the Son bore on the Cross. Although He is holy, He bore the sins of the world; indeed, He who knew no sin was made sin for us (2 Cor 5:21).

22.0.6.en: 5- The words of Christ here are not a question seeking an answer, nor a complaint, but an expression of the intensity of the sufferings He endures. These are not only the dreadful bodily sufferings and the psychological sufferings of everyone rising up against Him, so that even His beloved ones forsook Him, but the hardest of all these is the spiritual suffering of bearing, while He is the Holy One, all the sins of the world.

22.0.7.en: 6- By saying this on the Cross, Christ gives support to everyone who suffers and feels as if he were forsaken by God; Christ assures him that He feels with him and that he is not forsaken by Him.

22.0.8.en: 7- Christ said this verse in the Aramaic language, which the Jews understand, "Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani", in order to alert them that this Psalm, which the Jews memorize without understanding it, speaks about Christ, so that perhaps they might believe.

22.0.9.en: 8- Sin is the barrier that separates man from God. So Christ, on the Cross, bearing the sins of the world, expresses this by saying "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?" But when He completes redemption by His death, humanity obtains reconciliation with God in Him.

22.0.10.en: 9- The saying of Christ, "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?", is speech about humanity, which sinned against God, and on its behalf He speaks before the Father, although He is righteous and holy. He is a son of man but without sin, as He declared plainly to the Jews, saying, "Which of you convinceth me of sin?" (Jn 8:46), and therefore He does not deserve sufferings and death, but bears them for others, that is, fallen humanity, in order to save it from its sins. It is a declaration of His holiness, and that He did not deserve death or the Father's forsaking Him, but by His own will He accepts the sufferings. The hiding of the Father's face from Him is an expression of the divinity's distress at sin, in spite of its great love for humanity, which made Him become incarnate and unite with it, and suffer and die for it.

22.0.11.en: 10- A heresy appeared that proclaimed interpreting this verse as meaning that the divinity departed from the humanity. This is, of course, wrong; His saying this is a communion between the Son and the Father that expresses all the meanings mentioned above, that is, the perfection of Christ's humanity and the divinity's distress at sin. This verse expresses the work of the Second Hypostasis, the Son, in suffering for the sake of humanity and bearing its sins, and it also expresses the work of the Father, the just Judge, in leaving the Son to bear the sufferings unto death.

22.1.0.en: 2- O my God, I cry in the daytime, but thou hearest not; and in the night season, and have no rest.

22.1.2.en: 1- Here He affirms that He asks for God's help, but He does not answer Him, neither in the day nor in the night; that is, Christ's sufferings were continuous, whether in the day while on the Cross, or in the night while in the garden of Gethsemane, and He bore all this for our salvation.

22.1.3.en: 2- Asking for God's help in the day signifies asking at the time of victory, so that the believer may stand firm in his victory; while the night signifies tribulation, and the believer asks God to bring him out of it and to save him from his sufferings and troubles.

22.1.4.en: 3- God sometimes does not answer His children, because postponing their request is best, as in the case of Zacharias and Elizabeth, or because the request is not suitable for the salvation of the soul, such as the healing of St. Paul from his thorn; and at the same time He may answer the wicked, or even the demons, to their shame, as He answered the demons who begged that they might enter the herd of swine (Mt 8:31, 32). And in the case of Christ, the Father did not answer His prayer in the garden of Gethsemane that the cup of His sufferings might pass from Him, and left Him to bear the sufferings of the Cross, because the sins of humanity required that Christ bear these sufferings unto death, in order to redeem His children.

22.2.0.en: 3- But thou art holy, O thou that inhabitest the praises of Israel.

22.2.1.en: 1- Beginning with this verse, Christ presents a group of kinds of reproach to God for having forsaken Him. In this verse He reproaches God the Father, saying to Him: You are the Holy One in whom is the perfection of holiness and justice; how can You be content with injustice, and that the sins of the world be laid upon an innocent person?! This is an expression of the extent of the sufferings that Christ bears, confirming His humanity united with His divinity.

22.2.2.en: 2- God the Holy One is praised by His angels in heaven, but He also rejoices greatly in the praises of His children on earth, who were at that time His people Israel, since His people were the only people who believed in God.

22.2.3.en: 3- God is holy, that is, wholly holy, and therefore deserves praise from the heavenly and the earthly, for He alone is the Holy One. And all His holy children have received something of His holiness. These saints are the ones who appreciate holiness, and therefore they alone are the ones who praise Him. By the saints is meant everyone who believed in Christ and so became holy in Him.

22.3.0.en: 4- Our fathers trusted in thee: they trusted, and thou didst deliver them. 5- They cried unto thee, and were delivered: they trusted in thee, and were not confounded.

22.3.1.en: The second reproach of Christ to God the Father, on the lips of David by the spirit of prophecy: that when the fathers of God's people trusted in Him, prayed and cried to Him, He answered them and delivered them from their afflictions, as happened with God's people in Egypt, when He struck the Egyptians with the ten plagues and then drowned Pharaoh's army in the sea, and as He saved the three young men from the furnace of fire, Daniel from the lions' den, and chaste Susanna from the hands of the two elders.

22.4.0.en: 6- But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised of the people. 7- All they that see me laugh me to scorn: they shoot out the lip, they shake the head, saying,

22.4.1.en: 1- The third reproach that Christ presents to the Father is that He left Him until He became despised like the worm, which is trodden underfoot, and no longer had the dignity of a human being.

22.4.2.en: 2- The worm appears to be a very weak creature, just as Christ appeared in weakness during His crucifixion. This is how He appeared before men and the wicked Jews, who did not understand that it pleased the Father to bruise Him with grief. Christ by His own will accepted death, and accepted to appear as having no form nor comeliness, for the sake of our salvation. And while He appeared weak before men, in Him was the perfection of power, and by His death He abolished death and bound Satan.

22.4.3.en: 3- The worm, which appears very weak, is able to destroy the bodies of men, for it eats them after their death; and Christ on the Cross destroyed the old body, that is, the nature inclined to evil, and saved us from it and gave us the new nature by our birth in the sacrament of Baptism.

22.4.4.en: 4- The worm is the source of a red dye called crimson, and Christ shed His blood on the Cross, and by His blood, which is red in color, He gave redemption to all humanity, that we may be dyed with His dye and receive a new nature by His death and resurrection.

22.4.5.en: 5- There is a kind of worm called the hydra; if its body, which is formed of rings, is divided, each ring becomes able to live by itself. Likewise Christ, by His death, became the head of His body, which is the Church, and every member in it has its own independent life. Likewise, believers in Christ in the arenas of martyrdom become the cause of many believing in their God, and they too receive the crown of martyrdom.

22.4.6.en: 6- Isaiah prophesied about the people of Israel and described them as a worm (Isa 41:14). So God's people appeared weak at the captivity, like Christ on the Cross, but because God's power was with His children, He brought them back from the captivity, and from them came Christ, the Savior of the whole world.

22.4.7.en: 7- The worm comes out of the clay without mating; likewise Christ also was born like earthly man, but without the seed of man.

22.4.8.en: 8- By Christ's accepting the Cross, He became despised like the worm, indeed a reproach of men and despised of the peoples, so that the Jews, while He was on the Cross, mocked Him (Mt 27:42). How then can man, who is of dust and whom the worm eats, be proud and think that he is something and ascribe glory to himself, although all that he has is gifts from God?!

22.4.9.en: 9- The Jews who passed by the crucified Christ showed their evil and their contempt for Him, and mocked Him in every way; for they opened their mouths, "shooting out the lip", laughing at Him. They also "shook the head", that is, wagged their heads in contempt of Him (Mt 27:39). Thus their hard hearts were devoid of feeling and tenderness toward Him; moreover, their outward behavior was moved to abuse Him with the head and with the mouth. It is a marvelous hardness, especially because it came upon the Righteous and Holy One, who had wronged no one.

22.5.0.en: 8- "He trusted on the LORD that he would deliver him: let him deliver him, seeing he delighted in him."

22.5.1.en: 1- David the prophet foretold what the wicked Jews, who passed by the crucified Christ mocking Him, would say, saying that He is rejected by God; for if He were with God, let Him deliver Him from the sufferings of the Cross. Indeed, they said the very words that David prophesied (Mt 27:43).

22.5.2.en: 2- Satan speaks on the tongue of the wicked, to cast doubt on the righteous about their conduct and their life. By the righteous are meant those who believe in Christ, for when they see the crucified Christ in weakness they leave their faith. This satanic doubting is repeated every day until now, but the faith of those who believe in Christ remains firm, bearing sufferings unto death, in order to receive the power of the resurrection, which they feel in their lives on earth, that is, they feel peace and joy in fellowship with God, and then in eternity they enjoy the glories of the Kingdom of Heaven.

22.5.3.en: 3- The doubting of Christ was in two matters:

22.5.4.en: a - That He does not trust in God and does not believe in Him, otherwise He would have delivered Him from the Cross.

22.5.5.en: b - That He is not loved by God; He is not His beloved Son as He claims, otherwise He would have rescued Him from these sufferings.

22.6.0.en: 9- For thou art he that drew me out of the womb: thou didst make me secure upon my mother's breasts.

22.6.1.en: 1- In this verse David the prophet speaks by the spirit of prophecy about Christ, who makes the fourth reproach to the Father for having left Him to all these sufferings, although it is God who drew Him out of the womb and nursed Him at the breast of the Virgin His mother; so why does He forsake Him now? This confirms the humanity of Christ and that He bore real, hard sufferings.

22.6.2.en: 2- The Father is the one who drew Him out of the womb, because the birth of Christ was wonderful, distinguished from the rest of mankind in that it was without the seed of man, and it did not dissolve the virginity of the Virgin; God drew Him out of the womb, and the virginity of the Virgin remained sealed. This is the divine miracle.

22.6.3.en: 3- The Child Jesus nursed milk from His mother's breast, and was secure while nursing like any child, and this confirms His humanity and His need for nursing like the rest of mankind.

22.6.4.en: 4- The womb from which the Father drew the Son is also the Jewish nation, and He came out of it to redeem it and to redeem the whole world.

22.6.5.en: 5- If it is the Father who drew Him and set Him securely on His mother's breast, then He is responsible for His birth and His life on earth, and therefore He is responsible for the sufferings He endures; these insults from men are directed against the Father, and He trusts in Him. Likewise, a person who trusts in God feels that what he suffers, despite his good conduct, is directed at God, so he is not troubled; if God wills, let Him rescue him, or fight for him, and if it is for his good, He supports him to bear the sufferings.

22.6.6.en: 6- This verse also applies to every believer in the New Testament, whom God draws out of the womb of the Church, which is the baptismal font, and nurses him securely at the breast of his mother the Church, that is, satisfies him with her prayers, her books, her history, and all that she contains of rites and doctrines.

22.7.0.en: 10- I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother's belly.

22.7.1.en: Here He confirms the fourth reproach mentioned above, which is that He trusts in God, so why does He leave Him to bear all these sufferings? And here He declares that He was cast upon God from the time He was in the womb, in the Virgin's belly; He trusted in God throughout His life, indeed before His life began, while He was in the womb.

22.8.0.en: 11- Be not far from me; for trouble is near; for there is none to help.

22.8.1.en: 1- The reproach here turns into prayer, and Christ asks the Father not to be far from Him; for Christ as a man declares His need of the support of the divinity in order to bear the sufferings, just as every person in tribulation needs God in order to be able to bear it and pass through it.

22.8.2.en: 2- The secret of the strength of the believer within tribulation is God's being with him, so he accepts the pain, and even rejoices in his fellowship with God during the pain, and the pain turns into joy.

22.8.3.en: 3- Christ declares that trouble is near, and what is meant by it is death on the Cross, and this calls for divine help to pass through death, and then the resurrection.

22.8.4.en: 4- In the midst of the sufferings all men forsook Christ, and there was no helper except the Father; so every person feels that he needs God intensely in the midst of tribulation, so that he is not troubled if people part from him.

22.9.0.en: 12- Many bulls have compassed me: strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round.

22.9.1.en: Bashan: a region in Gilead lying east of the Jordan River, known for the fertility of its pastures, and therefore for its valuable, strong cattle and bulls.

22.9.2.en: Beset me round: surrounded me closely.

22.9.3.en: 1- Christ speaks of the wicked who surrounded Him and rose up against Him to crucify Him, and describes them as follows:

22.9.4.en: a - That their number is very great; for they were from the Jews and the Gentiles, because the priests stirred up the whole Jewish people, and the Gentiles appeared in Pilate and the soldiers under him.

22.9.5.en: b - That they are strong and overbearing toward Him, resembling the strong bulls of Bashan.

22.9.6.en: 2- And these bulls signify the priests who rose up against Christ, and the elders of the Jews and their rulers, and likewise the whole people, in addition to the fact that they also signify the Gentiles who rose up against Christ and crucified Him.

22.9.7.en: 3- Stray bulls, if they find a stranger, surround him, charge at him with their horns, and try to kill him; just as the Jews, who had strayed from the faith, charged at Christ, who was a stranger to their thoughts, and seized Him and delivered Him to Pilate to crucify Him.

22.10.0.en: 13- They gaped upon me with their mouths, as a ravening and a roaring lion.

22.10.1.en: Roaring: giving out strong, frightening sounds.

22.10.2.en: He describes the wicked Jews and the Gentiles who surrounded Christ at His arrest, torture and crucifixion as being like the ravening lion, which gives out strong, frightening sounds in order to pounce on its prey, that is, Christ. This happened when the Jews gathered before Pilate and cried out to him to crucify Him, saying, "His blood be on us, and on our children" (Mt 27:25). The comparison of Satan to a lion is repeated, as in (1 Pet 5:8; 2 Tim 4:17).

22.11.0.en: 14- I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint: my heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels.

22.11.1.en: 1- Human nature, by death, dissolves quickly, like the pouring out of water; so Christ expresses the sufferings and the death that will come upon Him and separate His soul from His body.

22.11.2.en: 2- Christ was poured out like water when He prayed fervently in the garden of Gethsemane as He was approaching His sufferings, and His sweat was as great drops of blood (Lk 22:44).

22.11.3.en: 3- When the soldier pierced Christ's side on the Cross, blood and water came out of Him (Jn 19:34) and was poured out on the ground; it is a literal fulfillment of this prophecy.

22.11.4.en: 4- The pouring out of Christ's life on the Cross like water shows the contempt of the wicked Jews for Him, and Christ accepted the shame of the Cross and the pouring out of His life, as something very cheap, out of His love for us, to redeem us.

22.11.5.en: 5- Water poured out on anything washes it and cleanses it; so by the pouring out of Christ's life on the Cross He cleansed those who believe in Him from their sins.

22.11.6.en: 6- When Christ's body was pierced with three nails, the body hung with all its weight on these nails, and this led to the separation of His bones from one another.

22.11.7.en: 7- The separation of Christ's bones does not only mean His death on the Cross, but also means that everyone scattered from Him, as He said to His disciples, "and shall leave me alone" (Jn 16:32), and most of His followers were dispersed, while the Apostles hid in the closed upper room for fear of the Jews (Jn 20:19). And because the Church is the body of Christ, if God's children who believe in Him are scattered and leave Him, they are like the bones in the body that are separated from one another; but at the same time God promises in the Psalm and says of the bones of the righteous that they are not broken, that is, God returns and gathers them again a second time (Ps 34:20).

22.11.8.en: 8- As the sufferings came upon Christ's body on the Cross, so also His inner feelings were sorrowful (His heart melted like wax) over His disciples who abandoned Him, indeed one of them sold Him and some of them doubted. He also grieved over the Jews who persisted in evil. For He feels that all are His children. And this "bowels" of His expresses His womb, which bore all these rebellious sons. But His fatherhood continued to pray for them while He was on the Cross, saying, "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do" (Lk 23:34).

22.11.9.en: 9- Wax melts by fire and heat, and this signifies that the soul of man is melted by suffering, so that it becomes pure from all evil, and then the image of Christ appears easily in this liquid wax. Therefore the believer does not fear tribulations, because they purify him and bring him near to God, and he becomes a clear image of Christ.

22.12.0.en: 15- My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death. Potsherd: a broken piece of pottery.

22.12.1.en: 1- A potsherd, if placed in the fire, dries out of any moisture in it. Likewise the life of Christ dried up in the furnace of the sufferings and sorrows that He bore.

22.12.2.en: 2- The tongue of Christ cleaved, that is, His mouth from the inside, as an expression of His silence before the many accusations falsely brought against Him by the wicked Jews. He bore all this for our sake and did not answer, because the hearts of the wicked were hard and did not wish to hear, and also as an expression of the suffering of His intense thirst.

22.12.3.en: 3- Christ went down into the dust of death in the tomb, and this is a wonderful humility and great love on His part, that He accepts death, being God, for our sake, we sinners. But death could not hold Him; rather, He rose on the third day. Therefore He said "the dust of death" and not "death", as an expression of His authority over death.

22.12.4.en: 4- The emptying of the will and obedience appear in Christ's submission to the will of the Father, who laid Him in the dust, although this is contrary to His divinity; but He accepted it as a man united with His divinity for the sake of our salvation.

22.13.0.en: 16- For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet.

22.13.1.en: 1- David speaks of the wicked Jews, whether the priests, or the scribes and Pharisees, or the people, and likens them to dogs that tear at Christ with their false accusations, their attempts to trap Him in a word, and then their demanding that Pilate crucify Him; by this they followed Satan.

22.13.2.en: 2- By dogs he also means the Gentiles who rose up against Christ, who were the Roman soldiers, and crucified Him. The Gentiles in the eyes of the Jews are considered dogs, as Christ expressed that at the healing of the daughter of the Canaanite woman (Mt 15:26); but when these Gentiles believed they became sons, while the Jews who refused to believe in Christ lost their sonship and followed Satan, so they became like dogs.

22.13.3.en: 3- The Cross is a Roman form of death devised by the Romans to torture criminals, but David the prophet, in whose time there was no use of the Cross, but only hanging on a tree, saw by the spirit of prophecy the Cross of Christ, and described accurately what would happen on it, the piercing of His hands and feet, to be hung on the Cross.

22.13.4.en: 4- The Jews thought that by crucifying Christ and piercing His hands and feet they had deprived Him of the ability to move, and prevented His works and words that exposed their sins. But by these nails He died for us and made the greatest movement in the world, for He saved humanity from its death, gave it new life, and bound Satan.

22.14.0.en: 17- I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me.

22.14.1.en: 1- When Christ was scourged, His flesh was torn away and His bones became clearly visible, so it became easy to count and number them, in addition to the fact that He was crucified naked and the Jews stared at Him, so they saw His bones and counted them. And Christ bore the sufferings of scourging and nakedness, and everyone looked at Him, and counted His bones, and despised Him. And He bore all this for us.

22.14.2.en: 2- If nakedness is a result of sin, as Noah was uncovered when he drank the wine (Gen 9:21) and the children of Israel were uncovered when they worshiped the golden calf (Ex 32:25), then Christ accepted to be naked for our sake, that is, He bore our sins and what accompanies them, to clothe us with the robe of His righteousness.

22.14.3.en: 3- When Christ was scourged and His flesh was torn away, His bones remained, and the bones signify the strong believers, while the flesh signifies the weak believers, who fall away before torments, but the bone remains firm in its place.

22.14.4.en: 4- When the Jews and the Gentiles examined the crucified Christ, they found Him being tortured although He was without sin, and because their hearts were evil they despised Him. But some of them had their minds enlightened and believed, because they saw that He was tortured while without sin, such as the right-hand thief, and the soldier who pierced Him with the spear, who is called Longinus, and the centurion who was in charge of the crucifixion.

22.14.5.en: 5- All these sufferings, the piercing of His hands and feet, the counting of His bones, and people's staring at Him, show the perfection of Christ's humanity; He suffered real sufferings, which answer all the heresies that reject the humanity of Christ.

22.15.0.en: 18- They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture.

22.15.1.en: 1- This verse too, which David prophesied, was fulfilled literally, and the Evangelists who witnessed the crucified Christ mention it (Jn 19:23, 24).

22.15.2.en: 2- The garment of Christ, that is, His tunic, was woven as one piece, so the Jews cast lots for it. And this tunic signifies the one faith delivered as a grace to God's children in His Church. And the idea of casting lots means that not everyone will receive this tunic, and this signifies that faith is given only to the chosen, who are saved, while the rest reject it and so do not receive it.

22.15.3.en: 3- And because Christ's garment is the faith, which cannot be divided, all believers accepted it except the heretics, who tore it, such as Arius, who tore the garments of Christ, as Pope Peter, the Seal of the Martyrs, saw Christ in a dream with His garments torn, and He told him that Arius is the one who tore His garments.

22.15.4.en: 4- The garments of Christ signify His teachings, and the soldiers divided them among themselves, and this signifies the spread of Christ's teachings, and the distinction of some believers with certain virtues, and others with other virtues.

22.16.0.en: 19- But be not thou far from me, O LORD: O my strength, haste thee to help me.

22.16.1.en: 1- Christ accepted all the sufferings, but He asks the Father not to be far from Him, for this is the necessary support that every believer in God wants in the midst of sufferings. And therefore he is able to bear the sufferings, and even be at peace and rejoice in God's presence.

22.16.2.en: 2- When He says "O my strength" He declares that God is His only hope and confidence, to be an example for us in our tribulations that we should rely on nothing except the power of God, which is able to solve all our problems.

22.16.3.en: 3- He also says "haste thee to help me", that is, raise me up quickly, and this shows the extent of the sufferings He endures, and His need of a swift resurrection, for this relieves Him of His sufferings and would be a support to His disciples who stumbled and doubted Him.

22.16.4.en: 4- The swiftness of the victory, that is, the swift resurrection on the third day, is a proof of His righteousness and divinity. And this signifies the feelings of the believer who suffers tribulation and needs God to raise him quickly from his sin and lift his tribulations from him.

22.17.0.en: 20- Deliver my soul from the sword; my only one from the hand of the dog.

22.17.1.en: 1- In the midst of the suffering of the Cross, Christ asks the Father to deliver His soul from the sword, and what is meant is the sufferings. This confirms His humanity and His bearing real, hard sufferings. The mention of the sword here is like what Simeon the elder said to the Virgin, that a sword would pass through her own soul, meaning the sufferings (Lk 2:35).

22.17.2.en: 2- By the sword is also meant the divine wrath deserved for the sins of men, which Christ bore on the Cross. And this soul of His is distinguished from the rest of human souls in that it is without sin.

22.17.3.en: 3- By "His only one" Christ also means the Church, so the Father delivers her from the wars of Satan.

22.18.0.en: 21- Save me from the lion's mouth, and from the horns of the wild oxen hear me.

22.18.1.en: 1- Christ also asks on the Cross to be saved from the lion's mouth, meaning Satan, as the Apostle Peter spoke of him (1 Pet 5:8).

22.18.2.en: 2- By wild oxen he means the wicked who take the appearance of the meek, like the tame ox, but in truth are savage and gore with their horns.

22.18.3.en: Do not be troubled by the wicked rising up against you, but cry out to God who is near you and able to rescue you from their hands. And if He allows you a tribulation, He is beside you, supporting you and giving you peace, and even joy as well.

22.19.s.en: (2) The thanksgiving of Christ the Savior

22.19.0.en: 22- I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee.

22.19.1.en: 1- Christ is the only Son who is in the bosom of the Father, who knows all things, and He alone is able to declare to us what belongs to the Father (Jn 1:18). And He declares to His brethren the name of God and proclaims to them the nearness of the Kingdom of Heaven, because He is the firstborn among many brethren (Rom 8:29). By His brethren are meant His disciples, His followers, and all mankind.

22.19.2.en: 2- The congregation is the Church that Christ founded with His blood. And by His Body and Blood on the altar He offers the greatest praise of love, and the believers in Him share with Him in the hymn of thanksgiving, that is, the sacrament of the Eucharist, which is the Divine Liturgy.

22.20.0.en: 23- Ye that fear the LORD, praise him; all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him; and fear him, all ye the seed of Israel.

22.20.1.en: 1- Christ asks those who fear the Lord to praise Him, and by those who fear Him is meant everyone among the Gentiles who fears God, for they used to call the devout Gentiles "those who fear the Lord", such as Cornelius (Acts 10:22).

22.20.2.en: 2- He calls the people of God, whom God blessed, as Isaac blessed Jacob, and says to them "ye the seed of Jacob", and asks them to glorify Him, because they know Him and know that He is the only God who deserves all honor and glorification.

22.20.3.en: 3- Christ asks the seed of Israel, who saw God and wrestled with Him and whose name He changed from Jacob to Israel, to fear God and revere Him, since Israel saw God and His majesty, and therefore the fear of Him came to be in his heart.

22.21.0.en: 24- For he hath not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted; neither hath he hid his face from him; but when he cried unto him, he heard.

22.21.1.en: 1- The man fallen into sin, who became poor and in need of God's help, when he cried to Him in lowliness, God had compassion on him, became incarnate, redeemed him, and gave him new life.

22.21.2.en: 2- The poor man is the humble person on whom God has compassion, so He rescues him and lifts him up, as our mother the Virgin declared that He "exalted the humble" (Lk 1:52).

22.21.3.en: 3- Christ our God emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, and being made in the likeness of men (Phil 2:7), so the title of the poor man applies to Him; all this He did for our salvation. Then His heavenly Father looked upon Him, and after He died and completed our redemption, He rose by the power of His divinity from the dead.

22.21.4.en: 4- The cry of the poor is very precious to God, so He does not hide His face from them but hastens to their help.

22.21.5.en: 5- God distinguishes the humble by showing His face to them, so they enjoy the sight of Him more than the rest of mankind. And seeing the face of God is better than everything in existence, and it is true life. Blessed are the humble, for they enjoy God's reign over their hearts in this age, in preparation for His eternal reign in heaven.

22.22.0.en: 25- My praise shall be of thee in the great congregation: I will pay my vows before them that fear him.

22.22.1.en: 1- Christ the Son says to the Father that just as the Father is praised and glorified, so also the praise and glorification of the Son will be proclaimed after He completes salvation on the Cross, and His resurrection and ascension. And this praise will be in the midst of the great congregation, which is the Church; that is, Christians in their churches praise their Christ, the Savior and Redeemer, after they have believed that He is God, who died for their salvation.

22.22.2.en: 2- Christ pays His vows by offering Himself on the Cross, because He promised the redemption and salvation of His people, and He fulfilled this and paid it on the Cross, and that was before all who feared Him and believed in Him.

22.22.3.en: 3- The effects of the sacrifice of the Cross extend, and we see the carrying out of God's promise to pay His vows on the altar every day, by offering His Body and Blood before those who fear Him, who are the priests of the New Testament, the deacons, and all who believe in Him and fear Him in the Divine Liturgy.

22.22.4.en: 4- The Apostles and all the servants of the New Testament went out to preach the paying of God's vows, that is, His promise of salvation to the whole world, before those who fear Him and have believed in Him, whether from the Gentiles or the Jews, so that they may enter His Church and enjoy His salvation.

22.23.0.en: 26- The meek shall eat and be satisfied: they shall praise the LORD that seek him: your heart shall live for ever.

22.23.1.en: 1- The meek are the humble and those who enjoy inner calm, and what is meant by them is the believers of the New Testament, who are those who cried to God, declaring their need in (v. 24), so He gave them salvation by faith in Him, and gave them also His Body and Blood in His Church, and satisfied them also with His word.

22.23.2.en: 2- The meek are also the poor in spirit, who are the sinners who repented and returned to God, so He gave them His Body and Blood, and satisfied them with His love. And this made them despise the lusts of the world and reject them.

22.23.3.en: 3- These meek, when a relationship is formed between them and God, ask His forgiveness and all their needs from Him, then advance in their spiritual life, so they praise Him and their hearts cling to Him, without any request of their own, but out of love for Him, and then continue in this praise, which always draws them to God, until their whole life turns into continual praise of Him, and through it they taste the Kingdom while still on earth.

22.23.4.en: 4- When the meek eat the Body and Blood of the Lord and praise Him and thank Him and are diligent in partaking of the Holy Mysteries, they abide in Christ and live for ever, that is, they enjoy the delight of life in Christ on earth, and then unspeakable glories in the Kingdom of Heaven.

22.23.5.en: 5- In summary, this verse speaks about the sacrament of Communion; whoever practices it is satisfied by it, and there is implanted in him a constant hunger and thirst for righteousness, so he is diligent in Communion and in everything that binds him to Christ. Then he seeks God in all his needs and renounces the world and does not depend on it. After that his heart is lifted up to the praise of God, and he continues in praise until his whole life becomes a hymn. And finally he receives eternal life in the Kingdom of Heaven.

22.23.6.en: If God's gifts toward you are continual, then the least you can do is thank Him for them every day, and when you thank Him you will feel the value of these gifts, so your praise and your contemplation of His love will increase, and you will love praise, and become a partner of the heavenly ones in enjoying fellowship with Him.

22.24.0.en: 27- All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the LORD: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee.

22.24.1.en: 1- David the prophet speaks by the spirit of prophecy about the New Testament, when the Gentiles believe in Christ and return to Him in repentance, to live with Him. The Gentiles will come to faith from every place in the world.

22.24.2.en: 2- When the believers who come from the Gentiles partake of Communion they rejoice and remember the crucified Christ who saves them, so He changes their lives and they imitate Him, and they come to have an inclination to self-giving and generosity.

22.24.3.en: 3- These converts from the Gentiles remember the name of the Lord, so their trust becomes in Him and they delight in fellowship with Him, because they remember Him every day and at all times, and so enjoy His presence.

22.24.4.en: 4- When these believers remember the name of God and live for Him, their conscience becomes good, that is, they recover the voice of God within them, so He speaks to them of God and establishes them in Him.

22.24.5.en: 5- After this they declare their submission to God and worship Him, so they seek His will and give up their own will, that is, they renounce the world and rejoice in obeying God's commandments, for they find their life in them.

22.25.0.en: 28- For the kingdom is the LORD'S: and he is the governor among the nations.

22.25.1.en: 1- When the peoples of the Gentiles abandoned the worship of idols and all that is connected with it, and submitted to God, He reigns over their hearts, and by His authority over them He gives them to enjoy His fatherhood and care.

22.25.2.en: 2- The natural state is that God reigns over the hearts of men, and sin caused man to lose this blessing, but by repentance and faith man regains God's reign over him. And God will help the Gentiles to repent; for no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Spirit (1 Cor 12:3).

22.25.3.en: 3- By God's reign over hearts, and His authority, He gives man a strong will able to control his senses, thoughts and feelings, which increases his enjoyment of God's reign over him, so he enjoys fellowship with Him.

22.26.0.en: 29- All they that be fat upon earth shall eat and worship: all they that go down to the dust shall bow before him: and he that hath not kept alive his own soul.

22.26.1.en: 1- The poor in spirit, that is, the repentant humble, who cried out to God and He answered them, and who believed and delighted in His Body and Blood, became fat, that is, spiritually filled with the Holy Spirit, who helped them to submit to God and worship Him.

22.26.2.en: 2- Not only the poor, the needy and those far off will eat of the Body and Blood of the Lord, but also the rich and the great who believe in God, and likewise the saints and those advanced spiritually; all eat and worship and enjoy higher degrees in the emptying of the will and in being satisfied with God.

22.26.3.en: 3- But the wicked who are bound to earthly things and who reject God, and therefore do not enjoy the working of the Body and Blood of the Lord in them, go down and bow and are buried in the dust of the grave, because they refused to keep their souls alive by the Holy Mysteries.

22.26.4.en: 4- The second part of the verse can also be interpreted by applying it to the humble who submit to God, so they worship Him down to the dust in many prostrations (metanoias), and so enjoy fellowship with God, and there joins them everyone who did not keep his soul alive with the pleasures and lusts of the world, that is, who renounced the world.

22.27.0.en: 30- A seed shall serve him; it shall tell of the Lord to the generation to come. 31- They shall come and declare concerning his Lord unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done

22.27.1.en: 1- He adds in this verse that the seed of the Gentile converts will serve God, that is, they will have a strong Church full of youth and vitality, as happened in Egypt, and they will be called children of God, that is, His offspring.

22.27.2.en: 2- Preaching will continue everywhere in the world, telling of God to the generation to come, that is, in the successive generations of the New Testament, so that many may believe and join the Church. And he says in (v. 31) "They shall come" and not "they came", that is, the preaching of Christ will be in the New Testament. And the priests of the New Testament and its servants speak of the righteousness of Christ, which saves sinners from their sins and justifies them.

22.27.3.en: 3- He tells us in (v. 31) of a people that shall be born, that is, a great number that will be born from the baptismal font and become a Church enjoying God's work in her.

22.27.4.en: 4- If the Jews rejected Christ and crucified Him, the Gentiles have believed in Him, but some Jews also believed, and many Jews will believe in Christ in the end, and they will bear a new people for God.

22.27.5.en: 5- If this Psalm began with the sufferings of Christ for us on the Cross, it ends with joy when the name of God the Holy One is proclaimed and many in the whole world believe in Christ.

22.27.6.en: God wants everyone to be saved, so He calls all to believe in Him. And you, do you call people by your life and conduct to live with God? Your love for all those around you, especially those who wrong you, shows the love of your Christ, so they believe in Him.

22.27.7.en: God the Shepherd "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want)" ... v. 1) Introduction:

22.27.10.en: When David was a shepherd; it is one of the first Psalms that David wrote.

22.27.12.en: At the coronation of kings; it was said on the way between the Temple and the spring of water, so that the king and all the people would remember the following:

22.27.13.en: a - That the king is of the offspring of David, the writer of this Psalm, who is a type of Christ.

22.27.14.en: b - That the true shepherd is God, and the instrument He uses is the king.

22.27.15.en: The newly baptized used to recite this Psalm after receiving the sacraments of Baptism and the Holy Myron, and before their Communion on the night of the Feast of the Resurrection.

22.27.16.en: 4- This Psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of the Third Hour, and it points to the work of the Holy Spirit in man, for it is He who supplies his needs, leads him, befriends him, and hosts him. Therefore some of the Fathers call it the Psalm of the Paraclete, because the waters of rest signify the waters of Baptism, and the table signifies the sacrament of the Eucharist.

22.27.17.en: 5- This Psalm is connected with the preceding Psalm, which speaks about Christ the Redeemer on the Cross; whoever believes in Christ the Redeemer receives the blessings of salvation that the Holy Spirit provides in this Psalm.
